dhp360:1: Restraint of the eye is good, restraint of the ear is good,
dhp360:3: Restraint of the nose is good, restraint of the tongue is good.
dhp361:1: Restraint of the body is good, restraint of speech is good,
dhp361:4: The monk who practices restraint in all things, obtains release from all suffering.
dhp362:1: He that controls his hands, he that controls his feet,
dhp362:2: He that controls his tongue, he that controls his head,
dhp362:3: He that delights in meditation, he that is well composed,
dhp362:4: He that is solitary and contented, such a man is truly called a monk.
dhp363:1: If a monk control his tongue, if he speak words of wisdom, if he be not puffed up,
dhp363:3: If he illuminate temporal and spiritual matters, the utterances of his lips will be pleasant to hear.
dhp364:1: He whose garden of delight is the Law, he that delights in the Law, he that ponders the Law,
dhp364:3: He that meditates upon the Law, that monk will never fall away from the Good Law.
dhp365:1: Let him not disdain what he has himself received, let him not envy others,
dhp365:3: For if a monk envy others, he will never attain Concentration.
dhp366:1: Though a monk receive but little, if he disdain not what he has himself received,
dhp366:3: The gods will praise him as of blameless livelihood, unwearied.
dhp367:1: He who has no attachment whatever for Name and Form,
dhp367:3: He who sorrows not for that which exists not, such a man is truly called a monk.
dhp368:1: That monk who abides in loving-kindness, and who has faith in the Religion of the Buddha,
dhp368:3: Will reach the Place of Peace, Cessation of Existence, Happiness.
dhp369:1: Monk, bale out this boat, for if it be baled out, light will it go for you.
dhp369:3: Destroy both lust and hatred; then to Nibbāna will you go.
dhp370:1: Cut off Five, renounce Five, develop Five more.
dhp370:3: The monk who has escaped from the Five Fetters is called “one who has crossed the flood.”
dhp371:1: Meditate, O monk, and be not heedless; permit not the pleasures of sense to sway your heart,
dhp371:3: Lest as a punishment for your heedlessness, you swallow the iron ball, lest you cry as you burn, “This is pain.”
dhp372:1: Meditation is impossible for him who lacks wisdom; wisdom is impossible for him who meditates not;
dhp372:3: He that both meditates and possesses wisdom is near Nibbāna.
dhp373:1: The monk who with tranquil heart enters an empty house,
dhp373:3: Experiences an unearthly delight through his right discernment of the Law.
dhp374:1: So soon as one grasps the thought of the rise and set of the Aggregates of Being,
dhp374:3: One obtains the happiness and joy of those who comprehend the Deathless.
dhp375:1: This is the proper way for a wise monk to begin in this world:
dhp375:2: Guarding of the senses, contentment, restraint under the Precepts;
dhp375:3: Cultivate virtuous friends, whose lives are pure, who faint not by the way.
dhp376:1: One should be cordial in manner, one should be upright in conduct;
dhp376:4: So will one experience profound joy and make an end of suffering.
dhp377:1: Even as the jasmine sheds its withered flowers,
dhp377:3: Even so, monks, should one shed lust and hatred.
dhp378:1: The monk who is tranquil in action, tranquil in speech, tranquil in thought, collected,
dhp378:3: Who has rejected the allurements of the world, he is truly called “composed.”
dhp379:1: Admonish thyself by thyself; examine thyself by thyself;
dhp379:3: Guard thyself; be mindful: do this, O monk! and thou shalt live in happiness.
dhp380:1: For self is the lord of self, self is the refuge of self:
dhp380:3: Therefore curb thyself, as a merchant curbs a goodly steed.
dhp381:1: Full of joy and satisfaction, the monk who has perfect faith in the Religion of the Buddha
dhp381:3: Will reach the Place of Peace, Cessation of Existence, Happiness.
dhp382:1: That monk who while still young devotes himself to the Religion of the Buddha,
dhp382:3: Such a monk illumines the world as does the moon freed from a cloud.
